title: From/Into Interface
concept: From and Into define type conversions. From is for explicit construction, Into is the reverse — `let x: Target = source.into()`.
why: Type conversions are everywhere. From/Into standardizes conversions, making your types interoperable with the ecosystem and eliminating boilerplate.
tips: Always implement From, never Into — Into is auto-derived from From
Use From for infallible conversions, TryFrom for fallible ones
From on newtypes makes your types feel native — `let email: Email = s.into()`
Implement From for common types that convert to yours — increase interoperability
common_mistakes: Implementing Into instead of From — the standard library provides blanket Into for any From
Using .into() without type annotation — the compiler needs to know the target type
Making From do validation that can fail — use TryFrom for fallible conversions
